newsitem.title: USA: U.S. money managers on hold for sales - MCM survey.
newsitem.headline: U.S. money managers on hold for sales - MCM survey.

text.p: U.S. fixed-income managers last week made few changes to their debt portfolios as they wait for Holiday sales clues, according to an MCM MoneyWatch Inc survey.

"Not a lot of shifts this week, or things away from prevailing trends," said MCM money market analyst Peter McTeague, who conducts the asset allocation survey. "Increasingly participants mention that rallying much further ... gets them to take money off the table. (Many money managers) are waiting for Holiday sales clues," he said.
The weekly survey showed durations as a percentage of benchmark rose to 108.1 percent in the week ended November 25 from 107.9 percent in the prior week.
A duration reading above 100 percent indicates the group of investors polled is mostly long on the market.
A portfolio's duration represents its average maturity and is used by portfolio managers to calculate exposure to risk.
In the "next likely move" category, portfolio managers representing 21 percent of total assets in the survey said they would "buy," down from 26 percent the prior week.
Strategists leaning toward "sell" rose to 32 percent, up from 28 percent in the week ended November 18.
Forty-seven percent of managers said they were "neutral" on the market, up from 46 percent a week ago.
Cash as a percentage of assets rose to 2.20 percent, against 2.12 percent registered the previous week.

The survey showed 26 percent of investors polled overweighted the 10-plus years duration sector, up from 23 percent the previous week, while 18 percent underweighted it. The remaining 56 percent were "neutral."
In the five- to 10-year duration sector, 49 percent of investors polled said they overweighted the securities and 7.0 percent underweighted them.
The survey included 40 domestic participants, who manage about $100 billion in fixed-income assets. The poll is conducted weekly by MCM and usually is released on Tuesday.
